_comment: Asian board for the 2026-09-11 slate (Taipei 09-12). Eleventh slate of the prospective test. All fifteen games on the US card, all legible with first-half totals. Fourth consecutive slate with no reading conflict: every favourite read off the rows agrees with the US moneyline, and the board's own moneyline column, shown in fourteen of the fifteen, agrees as well and has still never disagreed. The one game without it, White Sox at Cardinals, resolves on the market alone and matches: Chicago at 0.4907 with none of fourteen books above even. That game is also a correction to something recorded on 09-06. There I noted that the board printed the first-half handicap on Houston's row while the full-game handicap sat on Arizona's, and cited the mismatch as independent evidence that my full-game row read was wrong -- which it was, that time. Today the same mismatch appears here, first half on St. Louis and full game on Chicago, and this time the full-game row is the correct one. So that tell stands at one for two and is not evidence of anything; the moneyline is what decides, as the rule says. Handicaps flat at 0.950, totals flat at 0.940, no split prices.
